description: An asset that synchronously launches another Dagster job with config and waits for it to finish -- the Airflow TriggerDagRunOperator equivalent, Dagster-to-Dagster.

outputs.description: Metadata about the triggered run: triggered_run_id, triggered_job_name, success.

asset_key.label: Asset Key
asset_key.description: Dagster asset key for this trigger asset, slash-delimited (e.g. 'pipeline/trigger_downstream').

definitions_module.label: Definitions Module
definitions_module.description: 'pkg.module' or 'pkg.module:attr' (default attr 'defs') pointing at the target Definitions containing the job/assets to run.

job_name.label: Job Name
job_name.description: Name of an existing job in definitions_module to run. Set this or asset_keys, not both.

asset_keys.label: Asset Keys
asset_keys.description: Asset keys in definitions_module to run as an ad-hoc selection job. Set this or job_name, not both.

run_config.label: Run Config
run_config.description: Run config passed to the triggered run.

tags.label: Tags
tags.description: Extra tags on the triggered run (in addition to dagster-community/triggered-by).

partition_key.label: Partition Key
partition_key.description: Partition key for the triggered run, if the target job/assets are partitioned.

deps.description: Lineage-only upstream asset keys (no data passed at runtime).
deps.label: Deps

owners.description: Asset owners — team names (team:analytics) or email addresses.
owners.label: Owners

asset_tags.description: Key-value tags applied to the asset in the Dagster catalog, e.g. {"domain": "finance"}.
asset_tags.label: Asset Tags

kinds.description: Asset kinds shown in the Dagster catalog (e.g. snowflake, python). Auto-inferred from component name if empty.
kinds.label: Kinds

retry_policy_max_retries.description: Max retries on asset failure. Defines a RetryPolicy. Useful for transient network failures, rate limits, etc.
retry_policy_max_retries.label: Retry Policy Max Retries

pool.label: Pool
pool.description: Dagster's native named concurrency pool (e.g. Airflow's `pool` -- a fixed number of slots shared across every asset/op using the same pool name). The pool's own slot count is configured at the deployment level (dagster.yaml's concurrency: pools:, or the Dagster+ UI), not here.

timeout_seconds.label: Timeout Seconds
timeout_seconds.description: Fail this trigger asset if the triggered job hasn't finished after this many seconds. Enforced via a background-thread wrapper -- dagster.execute_job has no native timeout, and the triggered run is NOT terminated on timeout (Python threads can't be forcibly killed, and execute_job gives no run_id back until it returns); this only bounds how long the TRIGGERING step waits.

wait.label: Wait
wait.description: True (default): wait synchronously for the triggered job to finish -- Airflow's TriggerDagRunOperator(wait_for_completion=True). False: fire-and-forget -- create the run (a real run_id is returned immediately) and return, without waiting for it -- Airflow's wait_for_completion=False. The triggered run keeps executing in a background thread; this asset has no way to report its eventual success/failure (look it up by `triggered_run_id` in the Dagster UI/API). Mutually exclusive with `timeout_seconds` (nothing to time out if not waiting).

name: TriggerJobAsset
